prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose very first stake of the Church was organized between 1974 and 1976
prompts.text_original: From 1974 to 1976 the Church organized first stakes in Scandinavia, France and Chinese-speaking Asia. A country or territory whose very first stake of the Church was organized between 1974 and 1976.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Denmark, Sweden, France, Hong Kong, Taiwan)
prompts.note: The United Kingdom does not count: its first stake was in Manchester, England, in 1960.
prompts.summary: Copenhagen became the first stake in Scandinavia in 1974, and Stockholm and Paris followed in 1975. In April 1976 Taipei and Hong Kong received stakes within days of each other, the first in Chinese-speaking lands.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: The Copenhagen Denmark Stake, the first stake in Scandinavia, was organized June 16, 1974.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: The first stake in France was organized in Paris, November 16, 1975, with Gerard Giraud-Carrier as president.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: The Stockholm Sweden Stake was organized April 20, 1975, with Evert W. Perciwall as president.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: The Hong Kong Stake was created April 25, 1976, with Poon Shiu-Tat (Sheldon) as president.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: The Taipei Taiwan Stake was created April 22, 1976, with Chang I-ch'ing as first stake president.

prompts.display_text: Pin a continental Western European country (not Luxembourg or a microstate) that recognized the Church, 1952 to 1974
prompts.text_original: After World War II, the Church sought official legal standing from European governments so it could own property and operate freely. One of nine continental Western European countries (Portugal, Spain, France, Italy, Switzerland, Austria, Germany, Belgium or the Netherlands) whose government officially recognized the Church between 1952 and 1974.
prompts.note: Switzerland (1864) and Italy (1993) recognized the Church outside these years, so they do not count.
prompts.summary: In the decades after World War II, Western European governments gave the Church legal standing one by one: France in 1952, West Germany in 1953, Austria and the Netherlands in 1955, Spain in 1968 and Portugal in 1974. Recognition let the Church own meetinghouses, hold meetings openly and bring in missionaries.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: West Germany recognized the Church as a public-law corporation, December 7, 1953.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: France registered the Church as a foreign association in September 1952.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Spain officially recognized the Church, October 22, 1968.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: Austria granted the Church legal recognition, September 27, 1955.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: The Netherlands recognized the Church, August 22, 1955, after 19 years of requests.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: David M. Kennedy secured official recognition in Lisbon in 1974.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a land or people named in the book of Daniel, from Babylon to Grecia
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a land, city or people named in the book of Daniel (Babylon, Shushan by the river Ulai, Media and Persia, Grecia, Egypt, the Libyans and the people of Cush, the Nile land south of Egypt, Edom, Moab and Ammon, the ships of Chittim, and the glorious land)
prompts.note: Bible Ethiopia (Cush) lay in today's Sudan, so Sudan counts for Daniel 11:43. Jerusalem is scored as Israel.
prompts.summary: Daniel was taken captive to Babylon, served under Babylonian and Persian kings, and saw visions at Shushan. His visions trace Media and Persia, Grecia, and the long struggle of the kings of the north and south, which touches Egypt, Libya, Ethiopia, Edom, Moab, Ammon and the ships of Chittim (Dan 1-11).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Daniel was carried to Babylon in the land of Shinar (Dan 1:1-2).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: The king of the south of Daniel 11 rules Egypt (Dan 11:8, 42).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Daniel saw his vision at Shushan by the river of Ulai, and the ram stood for the kings of Media and Persia (Dan 8:2, 20).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Daniel prayed toward Jerusalem, and the king of the north enters the glorious land (Dan 6:10; 11:41).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: The rough goat is the king of Grecia (Dan 8:21).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Edom, Moab and the chief of the children of Ammon escape out of his hand (Dan 11:41).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: The Libyans shall be at his steps (Dan 11:43).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The king of the north stands in the glorious land and plants his palace in the glorious holy mountain; that land includes the hill country now in the West Bank (Dan 11:16, 41, 45).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: The ships of Chittim come against the king of the north (Dan 11:30); Chittim is Cyprus.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: The Ethiopians shall be at his steps (Dan 11:43); Bible Ethiopia (Cush) was the Nile land south of Egypt.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place in Josiah's reforms, his death at Megiddo, or Pharaoh Necho's march
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place or kingdom named in Josiah's reforms and death and their aftermath (2 Kings 23; 2 Chronicles 35-36): the high places of the gods of Zidon, Moab and Ammon, Bethel and Samaria's high places, Megiddo, Necho's march against the king of Assyria toward Carchemish by Euphrates, Riblah in Hamath, Egypt, Babylon, and the kingdom of Persia
prompts.note: Bethel and Samaria are in the West Bank (Palestine); Megiddo is in Israel.
prompts.summary: King Josiah of Judah purged idolatry from Jerusalem to Bethel and the cities of Samaria. When Pharaoh Necho marched north toward Carchemish to aid the king of Assyria, Josiah met him at Megiddo and was slain. Necho then bound Josiah's son Jehoahaz at Riblah and carried him to Egypt (2 Kgs 23; 2 Chr 35).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Pharaoh-nechoh king of Egypt came up, and he carried Jehoahaz to Egypt, where he died (2 Kgs 23:29, 34).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Josiah went against Necho and was slain at Megiddo (2 Kgs 23:29; 2 Chr 35:22-24).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Josiah broke down the altar at Bethel and the high places in the cities of Samaria (2 Kgs 23:15, 19).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Necho went up against the king of Assyria, whose homeland was on the Tigris (2 Kgs 23:29); Nebuchadnezzar later carried Jehoiakim and the temple vessels to Babylon (2 Chr 36:6-7).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Josiah defiled the high places Solomon had built for Chemosh of the Moabites and Milcom of the children of Ammon (2 Kgs 23:13).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Necho put Jehoahaz in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath (2 Kgs 23:33).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: The captives served in Babylon until the reign of the kingdom of Persia, when Cyrus king of Persia proclaimed the return (2 Chr 36:20-23).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: He also defiled the high place Solomon built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Zidonians (2 Kgs 23:13).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Necho came to fight against Carchemish by Euphrates (2 Chr 35:20); the ruins of Carchemish lie at Turkey's border with Syria; Church Bible Maps 5, 6 and 9 plot Carchemish on the upper Euphrates.
